relevance_note: Case report of one woman with Alexander disease and a de novo GFAP variant: "A novel heterozygous three-base duplication mutation (c.726_728dupAGG) in exon 4 of GFAP was identified".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand (no tables, no supplement); a small Python script only assembled the JSON. In scope: the single patient ('patient'); her two parents, tested negative, sex not stated ('parent of patient', 'parent of patient 2'), with no phenotype rows (described only as 'healthy parents'); and one previously published person given only by variant ('the case with R124_L125insQLR', label 'unnamed person 1', no reference number printed; Figure 1f legend cites the Waisman website for references). The text implies that case was adult-onset ('Our case is the second report of adult-onset AxD with an in-frame mutation') but no contiguous span states it for that person, so onset is left not reported. Y242D and A244V are named as previously reported mutations without any person, so no rows. Patient onset is given only as '5 years earlier' relative to the 27-year-old presentation; age_at_onset_iso8601 left null rather than computing 22 years. PROVEAN 'deleterious' prediction and absence from ExAC/HGVD are in silico/population evidence, not functional assays; functional_evidence_statement left not reported. 'No family history of neurological disorders' is not recorded as a feature of any person. Hyperreflexia (right Achilles) marked as a pyramidal sign; 'mild cognitive impairment' (MOCA-J 23/30) marked as cognitive decline. Periventricular white matter lesions were not treated as a 'periventricular rim'. 'Eye spot' sign is stated only for typical elderly-onset cases, not recorded for the patient. No contradictions found.
